No WAI-ARIA pattern covers a color picker, so UI SDK builds it from ones that do. The picker is a group. The area’s thumb and each slider thumb are sliders, and the area’s thumb names both of its channels, like “Saturation 76%, Brightness 96%”. The presets are a listbox, and each preset and the swatch are named by their color, like “vivid blue”.

The trigger in the popover example says the current color in its name. Thumbs grow while you drag only when motion is allowed, and the checkerboard, rings and focus outlines switch to system colors in forced colors mode.

The value is a CSS color string. Every part edits the same color, so use only the parts you need. `ColorPickerArea` and `ColorPickerSlider` render their thumb for you. Name the picker with `aria-label`, or with the label of a field around it.
UI SDK adds a little CSS of its own in a cascade layer named `ui-sdk`. Declare that layer at the top of your global stylesheet, above the Tailwind import, so your classes win over it.
UI SDK reads the direction from the page, so the area, the sliders and the arrow keys mirror. The inputs pick their own direction, so a hex value still reads left to right.

With `readOnly`, the thumbs stay focusable and the value is submitted, but drags, keys and typing leave the color alone.
With `space="oklch"`, add `ColorPickerAreaCanvas` to paint the area. Colors outside the screen’s gamut stay clear, and a thumb dragged there settles on the closest color inside when you let go.
`ColorPickerPopover`, `ColorPickerTrigger` and `ColorPickerContent` wrap the UI SDK popover. The content opens in the browser’s top layer, so it needs no portal.

`ColorPickerSwatches` is one tab stop with arrow keys between presets, and a preset stays selected however the value is written. `ColorPickerChannelInput` edits one channel as a number. The eyedropper hides itself in browsers that can’t pick from the screen.
`onValueChange` runs on every step of a drag, and `onValueCommit` once when it ends, so save there. A controller from `createColorPickerController()` sets the color from anywhere.
